extracted.intended_audience: general readers; authors, publishers, and others interested in the National Book Award process and history
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, procedures, categories, and selection criteria for the National Book Awards (U.S.), including nomination rules, panel composition, eligibility windows, stages (longlist/finalists/winners), and lifetime-award criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories (annual one-winner-per-category)
rubrics_metrics.description: National Book Awards are given to one book (author) annually in each of five categories: fiction, nonfiction, poetry, translation, and young people's literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There have previously been many other categories but they have been retired or subsumed in the existing five. The Foundation also presents two lifetime achievement awards each year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination eligibility — publishers only
rubrics_metrics.description: Only publishers nominate books for the National Book Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panelists may request particular nominations from publishers. A publisher must complete a nomination in the spring and mail copies to the panelists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual publication eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: A book must be published 'between December 1 of the previous year and November 30 of the current year' to be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 1984 the NBA have been presented in the fall, usually November, to books published roughly during the calendar year (December of the previous year through November).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging panel size and composition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges include writers, librarians, booksellers, and literary critics; beginning in 2013 panels were expanded to include experts in the literary field in addition to established writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection stages and timelines (longlist, finalists, winners)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation uses a multistage selection process: a longlist, a finalists list, and winners announced at the ceremony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginning in 2013 a National Book Awards longlist—announced in September and consisting of ten titles per category—precedes the finalists list, announced in October and comprising five titles per category; winners are announced at the November ceremony. Each panel considers hundreds of books each year; panelists read all valid nominees and compile shortlists in September.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of finalists per category
rubrics_metrics.description: Each category's finalists list comprises five titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fixed number five finalists was retained through 2012 and continues as the finalists list of five titles announced in October; longlist introduced in 2013 provides a preceding list of ten per category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translated Literature category eligibility and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Book Award for Translated Literature (added in 2018) recognizes works in translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2018 translation award is for living translators and authors and for fiction and non-fiction. (Previously, a translation award ran 1967–1983 but did not require the author to be living and was for fiction only.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and monetary prizes for finalists and winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalists and winners receive cash and physical awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each finalist receives $1,000, a medal, and a citation written by the judging panel; winners get $10,000 and a bronze sculpture. The Medal for Distinguished Contribution (a lifetime award) comes with a $10,000 cash prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medal for Distinguished Contribution — lifetime award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medal for Distinguished Contribution to American Letters is a lifetime achievement award presented by the Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It recognizes someone who 'has enriched [American] literary heritage over a life of service, or a corpus of work.' Presented at the final ceremony; historically many medalists have been previous NBA winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literarian Award — lifetime service criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Literarian Award for Outstanding Service to the American Literary Community is a lifetime achievement award presented annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It recognizes 'an individual for outstanding service to the American literary community, whose life and work exemplify the goals of the National Book Foundation to expand the audience for literature and to enhance the cultural value of literature in America.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges' ability to request nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Panelists may request particular nominations from publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although only publishers may formally nominate, judges can request publishers submit specific titles for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recent eligibility policy change — citizenship requirement removed
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2024 the National Book Foundation announced the awards would no longer require U.S. citizenship for eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically, since 1950 the awards were presented to American authors for books published in the United States; the 2024 change aligns eligibility with more recent shifts such as the Pulitzer's change.
